subject: Re: Data retention / deletion SLAs & SOC 2 details (post-demo follow-up)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@amayahealth.com>
Cc: security@amayahealth.com
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: data retention & SOC 2 items

Hi Jordan — thanks again for your time on the call today. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed so you have everything in one place.

1) SOC 2: Redwood is currently SOC 2 Type II in progress for the controls covering our hosted API and control plane. We can share the SOC 2 summary and the expected timeline for the Type II report (target: Q4 2026). Attached: Redwood_SOC2_Summary.pdf.

2) Vendor security questionnaire: I’ve attached our vendor security questionnaire response template (Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_Redwood.json) — feel free to send your questionnaire and we’ll start populating.

3) Data retention / deletion SLAs (summary):
   - Primary customer data (models/input/outputs you send to our hosted API): normal retention is 30 days for customer-initiated data in active storage unless contractually agreed otherwise.
   - Immediate deletion requests: we aim to remove data from active storage within 48 hours where possible; full removal including indexes and application-level traces typically completes within 30 days.
   - Backups & snapshots: backups are retained for 90 days by default; immutable snapshots used for disaster recovery are retained for up to 180 days depending on the retention policy we sign in the contract.
   - Audit/log retention: request/trace logs (used for debugging and billing) are retained for 365 days by default; we can scope shorter retention for EU customers on request (GDPR considerations).

4) GDPR/HIPAA: Redwood supports data processing agreements and can sign a BAA where required. For HIPAA workflows, we recommend Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) to minimize exposure of PHI in shared infrastructure — happy to loop in our compliance lead for a short technical session.

Next steps we agreed:
- You to share Amaya’s security questionnaire and any specific retention requirements (especially for backups and immutable snapshots).
- I’ll pull Rishi (security) & Dev (engineering) into the thread to provide precise SLA language and retention windows for backups and log deletion.
- Schedule follow-up (15–30m) to review questionnaire responses and finalize any contract language.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_Summary.pdf, Data_Retention_SLA_Table.xlsx, Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_Redwood.json

Thanks — Marissa

Thanks Marissa — super helpful summary. A few clarifying Qs from our security team so we can fill the questionnaire: 

1) When you say backups retained for 90 days, are those backups encrypted with separate KMS keys per tenant? Are deletion requests propagated to backups, or do backups require separate lifecycle requests?

2) For the 48-hour target for removal from active storage, can you confirm what is included: immediate (soft) deletion vs. secure deletion/overwriting? We need to understand how long PHI might still reside in any system storage or cache.

3) Audit/logs retention of 365 days — can that be shortened to 90 days for our account? If so, what is the lead time and are there any impacts to billing/usage reconciliation?

Would appreciate short, discrete answers we can paste into our questionnaire. If easier, we can take the 15–30m follow-up next week.

—Jordan

Hi Jordan — looping in Rishi (security) and Dev Patel (engineering) to answer these specifically. Short answers below, attaching a small SLA table for copy/paste (Data_Retention_SLA_Table.xlsx).

1) Backups & KMS: Backups are encrypted at rest using envelope encryption. We support customer-managed keys (CMK) via KMS for Private deployments; for hosted customers we currently offer account-level CMKs in supported regions. Backups are tenant-scoped but stored in our managed backup system — deletion requests do not immediately remove historical backups; backups follow the configured backup lifecycle. We can include a contract clause to shorten backup retention or to trigger secure purge within X days for agreed accounts.

2) Deletion semantics: The 48-hour target refers to removal from active indexes and application-level storage (soft + dependent caches). Secure deletion/crypto-shredding from all replicated storage and caches is typically within 30 days; for cryptographic key destruction (where applicable) we can provide additional guarantees for Private deployments.

3) Audit/log retention: We can offer account-specific retention policies. Shortening to 90 days is possible — it requires a 30-day lead time to change retention pipelines and has no impact on billing reconciliation (we retain aggregated billing metrics separately for invoicing).

Rishi/Dev — can you confirm the exact phrasing we should provide in the questionnaire re: backups (encryption + lifecycle) and the timeline for immutable snapshot purge?

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Jordan — added a few precise lines you can paste into your questionnaire: 

• Backups: All backups are encrypted at rest using AES-256 envelope encryption. For hosted customers, backups are encrypted with Redwood-managed keys; customer-managed keys (CMKs) via KMS are available for Dedicated and Private deployments or for hosted customers in supported regions upon request. Backups are tenant-scoped and retained per the configured backup lifecycle. By default backups are retained for 90 days; immutable snapshots used for DR are retained up to 180 days. Contractual provisions can shorten these windows or enable on-demand purge for specific accounts with reasonable notice.

• Deletion SLA: Upon customer-initiated deletion request, Redwood will remove data from active production indexes and application storage within 48 hours. Complete cryptographic removal from all replicas and backups is completed within 30 days under normal operating procedures. For customers requiring accelerated crypto-shredding, Redwood offers a Private deployment option and can include specific timelines in the contract.

• Audit/log retention: Default retention for request/trace logs is 365 days. Customer-specific retention windows (e.g., 90 days) can be enabled with a 30-day implementation lead time. Billing/usage reconciliation is retained in aggregated form to support invoicing and does not require raw log retention.

If you want, we can add the three bullets above directly into the questionnaire file and send an updated copy.

—Rishi
